chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdul Rahman ibn Salim, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Who washed Fatima (peace be upon her)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That was Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' It was as if you were astonished by his words, so he said to me, 'It is as if you are constricted by what I informed you.' So I said, 'That was it, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said to me, 'Do not be constricted, for she was a truthful one (Siddiqah). None washed her except a truthful one. Do you not know that Maryam (peace be upon her) was not washed except by Isa (peace be upon him)?'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so what do you say regarding the woman who is in travel with men, having no Mahram (close male relative) with them, nor a woman with them, and the woman dies? What should be done with her?' He said: 'Wash from her what necessitates Tayammum, and she is not touched, and nothing of her beauty (Mahasin) which Allah (Exalted and Mighty) commanded to be covered is uncovered.' I said, 'How is it done with her?' He said: 'The palm of her hands is washed, and her face, and the back of her hands is washed.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for washing a woman who dies during travel without a Mahram or another woman present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual washing (Ghusl) of a woman who dies in travel without a Mahram or another woman, establishing that only the parts required for Tayammum (face and hands) are uncovered and washed to preserve modesty. It further contextualizes this by referencing the washing of Fatima (peace be upon her) and Maryam (peace be upon her), with the Imam noting that only a 'Siddiq' (truthful one) washed them, highlighting the spiritual status of the washers. This ruling is derived from the principle of maintaining the 'mahasin' (beauty/modesty) of the body, ensuring minimal exposure during the ritual.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, from Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Who washed Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>’. It was as if I was astonished from his<sup>asws</sup> words, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is as if you are constricted from what I<sup>asws</sup> informed you’. So I said, ‘It was that, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do not be constricted, for she<sup>asws</sup> is a truthful. None could have washed her<sup>asws</sup> except for a truthful. Do you not know that Maryam<sup>as</sup>, none washed her<sup>as</sup> except for Isa<sup>as</sup>?’

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! So what are youasws saying regarding the woman who happens to be in the journey with the men, there not being anyone with sanctity for her with them, nor is there a woman with them, and the woman dies. What should be done with her?’ Heasws said: ‘He would wash from her what Allahazwj Obligated the Tayammum upon, and she would neither be touched nor anything being uncovered from her beauty which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Commanded with its concealment’. I said, ‘How would he deal with it?’ Heasws said: ‘He would wash the inside of her palms, and her face, and he would wash the back of her palms’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Who gave Ghusl (bath) to Fatimah, ‘Alayha al- Salam ? He (the Imam) said, ‘That was ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. It seems as if you find it astonishing to hear such words.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘It seems you are strained because of what I told you.’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, that is true.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘You must not be stressed out; she was a truthful one and no one other than a truthful one could give her Ghusl (bath). Consider the case of Maryam (Mary) who was given Ghusl (bath) by no one other than Jesus, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’

I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what do you say about the case of a woman who dies during a journey in the company of men among whom there is no one of her relatives or other woman. What they must do?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Only those parts of her body are washed which Allah has made obligatory to be used for Tayammum. She is not touched and neither anything of her beauty which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has covered must be exposed.’ I then asked, ‘What they must do?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Only her palms, face and the backs of her hands are washed.’”
